_README: Which steps survive when the system cannot afford to run everything.
Read by core/survival_mode.py. Like config/scheduler.json this file is
HUMAN-tunable only: a system that can promote its own steps to CRITICAL has
no priority table. Two values, and no third — a scale invites the brain to
argue about the middle.
CRITICAL  runs even in survival mode. Losing it either breaks the audit
chain or leaves the day with no measurement at all.
NORMAL    skipped in survival mode. Everything else. NORMAL is the
default, so a step added to the cycle and forgotten here is
skipped under stress rather than silently protected.
PRIORITY IS NOT THE SAME QUESTION AS DEGRADATION. A CRITICAL step may still
come out DEGRADED through core/step_budget.py — CRITICAL means 'attempt it',
not 'it must succeed'. The only thing priority buys a step besides being run
at all is access to the 8b model tier.
HOW THIS LIST WAS DERIVED, so the next reader can argue with it:
12 of the 16 are exactly the steps core/cycle_map.py already marks
backbone=True — a curated list that predates this file and means 'not
skippable by opinion; the audit chain does not break'. Reusing it rather
than inventing a second opinion about the same question.
The other 4 are the snapshot steps, named directly in the survival-mode
brief (scoring, snapshot, merkle commit, cycle_report). They are NOT
backbone, because a cycle whose audit chain is intact can still be missing
a night of snapshots — but a survival day that measures nothing has
nothing for the scorer to score, so under stress they are what the day is
FOR.
FLAGGED FOR HUMAN REVIEW: brain_briefing, self_mirror and brain_debrief are
CRITICAL here because they are backbone, but all three are LLM-heavy and
survival mode is usually entered BECAUSE the models are unreachable. They
will most often run and degrade. Kept CRITICAL because breaking the audit
chain is the worse failure — but this is the entry most likely to be wrong,
and it is a human's call, not the system's.
